title: Chapter XXXV
summary: St. John's cold disapproval nearly crushes Jane more effectively than anger. She sees that as his wife his principled hardness would kill her without malice, while Diana confirms that India and his demands would destroy her physically. During his final appeal, St. John's prayer and moral certainty almost persuade Jane to merge her will into his. Asking for a true sign, she hears Rochester's distant voice call her name in pain. The call breaks St. John's ascendancy; Jane commands solitude, prays in her own way, and resolves to discover Rochester's fate.
events: St. John punishes Jane's refusal through controlled estrangement while continuing to press marriage.
Jane and Diana identify the physical and emotional destruction the proposed union would cause.
St. John's scriptural appeal nearly convinces Jane that marriage is God's will.
Jane hears Rochester call her name across an unknown distance and resolves to seek him.

characters.name: Jane Eyre
characters.development: Resists a second form of self-loss: not passion without principle, but duty without love; she recovers her own spiritual judgment.

characters.name: St. John Rivers
characters.development: His sincere zeal becomes coercive as he equates obedience to his plan with salvation and Jane's refusal with perdition.

characters.name: Edward Rochester
characters.development: Returns as a disembodied call whose suffering reactivates Jane's chosen bond when she is closest to renouncing it.

threads.text: Jane refuses marriage to St. John and abandons the India plan.
The novel's motif of sympathy across distance becomes an apparent call from Rochester.
Jane will investigate Rochester now that she can approach as an independent woman.
